in_hebrew.name: קָאר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: קָאר הוא שֵם הַנֶפֶשׁ, קָאר יָפֶה, מְגִנָּה, מַגֶן, מַשְׁמֶה, מָגִין. השם קאר נמצא בטקסט עברי כבר בתקופה הביזנטית.

in_greek.name: Κάρης
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κάρης προέρχεται από την αρχαία ελληνική λέξη καρής, που σημαίνει απάντηση. Στη βυζαντινή εποχή, το όνομα Κάρης ήταν κοινό στη Βενετία και σε άλλες πόλεις της Ανατολικής Μεσογείου.

in_latin.name: Carius
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Carius originem duxit ex verbo carere, quod significat respondere. In ecclesia primitiva, nomen Carius fuit commune in civitate Venetiarum et in aliis urbibus Mediteraneae Orientalis.

in_english.name: Kare
in_english.long_meaning: The name Kare originates from the Latin word carere, meaning response. In early Christianity, the name Kare was common in Venice and other cities of the Eastern Mediterranean. Kare is associated with the qualities of a hireling, one who responds to the call of duty, and greater, indicating a higher spiritual calling.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Kare' has cultural significance beyond its Greek roots. The name reflects the desire for purity and clarity in various aspects of life, including relationships, personal aspirations, and societal values. Its connection to Greek mythology and the biblical character Karis highlights a tradition of honoring the divine aspects of human nature. The name continues to resonate with modern-day Christians, reminding them of the importance of striving for purity in their own lives and in the world around them.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'Kare' is significant as it represents the inherent divine nature within each individual. The name encourages the pursuit of a pure and holy life, reflecting the image of God. The concept of 'pure air' in Greek mythology is a reminder of the transformative power of the Holy Spirit to cleanse and purify our lives from the inside out. The name Karis in the Bible also serves as a reminder of the importance of a noble and honorable character in the eyes of God. Ultimately, the name 'Kare' highlights the Christian belief in the capacity for personal transformation and the call to live a life grounded in purity and holiness.
